solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In the back of the car, brown, half shut brolly

indicators.note: the brown and the shut pieces go in the car's back, so this word signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a car's boot is its rear luggage space
umber is a brown earth pigment

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word shut is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a half-closed brown umbrella into the back of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: A car's boot is the British name for its trunk; 'In' signals the other pieces go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumbershoot is a jocular American word for an umbrella, and brolly is the British slang equivalent.

clue.text: Element I'm not sure will support posh queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so this hesitation comes last

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U
a rani is a Hindu queen
um is the noise of someone hesitating, unsure

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker wonders whether an element can prop up a grand queen.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive metal is a chemical element, number 92 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Spit broth etc out on top of everything

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of broth etc are rearranged
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook spits out broth and other things over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like a verb but is the noun: a skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochette is a skewer for cooking meat over heat, the kind of rod also called a spit.

clue.text: That man in pub is up for recovery

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the man is placed within the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man in a pub is getting back on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'is up' reads BHEAR from the bottom upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, a period of treatment for getting well again.

clue.text: Woman's order to wrap up is daring

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: the order is to enclose the other piece, as wrapping surrounds a parcel

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: A woman's command is to bundle up, which seems bold.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of 'Woman's' is read as a separate word 'is', which the order then wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is great courage, the noun sense of daring as boldness.

clue.text: A courgette at first wrapped in plain ham

indicators.note: the a and the courgette's first letter go inside the plain word

parts.note: overt means plain, open to view

indicators.note: this takes the opening letter of courgette

explanation.surface: A recipe: courgette wrapped in a slice of plain ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat; it is the verb for bad acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated theatricality, the same as to overact.

clue.text: Ache over defeat in a novel that's overly optimistic

indicators.note: in a down clue the ache sits above the defeat

parts.note: a pang is a sharp ache
a loss is a defeat

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of in a are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone feels pain about a defeat described in a cheerful novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pangloss is the relentless optimist in Voltaire's novel Candide, so 'novel' also hints at the source.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Dr Pangloss, who believed all is for the best, so it means naively cheerful.

clue.text: Ordinal away, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: this signals a word spoken that matches another in sound

parts.note: forth means away, onwards, as in go forth

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a number sounds distant.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal number gives position in a series, like first, second, third and the next one along.

clue.text: Love has passed by a very old libertine, one heavily stoned?

indicators.note: the love has gone past the other pieces, so it ends up after them

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rake
love is zero in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Love has walked past an elderly rake who is very drunk or high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests drugs; the fruit has one large stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped fruit holds a single big seed, so it is playfully heavily stoned.

clue.text: Set point after fast runner nets backhand, finally

indicators.note: the point comes after the rest
to net is to catch, so the runner holds a letter inside

parts.note: a hare is a fast-running animal

indicators.note: this takes the last letter of backhand

parts.note: N is north, a compass point

explanation.surface: A tennis set where a quick player wins with a backhand into the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words (set, point, nets, backhand) are all misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to become solid, as concrete or jelly firms up.

clue.text: Suggested incomplete part is noxious?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a part that is not the whole

explanation.surface: A partial suggestion is called harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word: SOME that is UN-WHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwholesome means bad for health or morals, which is what noxious describes.

clue.text: Tasteless sandwiches needing, primarily, parsley perhaps?

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between, so one letter goes inside the tasteless word

parts.note: garish means gaudy, tasteless

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of needing

explanation.surface: Bland sandwiches that need some parsley above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a typical example of a decoration placed on food.

clue.text: What's great, mind, about it?

indicators.note: the mind goes around the it

parts.note: the brain is the seat of the mind

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is so wonderful about the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is called Great, as in Great Britain, so it is the thing that is great.

clue.text: Initially, old German half as mysterious as ancient writing system

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next five words are taken

explanation.surface: An old German script is half as mysterious as an ancient writing system.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an early medieval Irish alphabet of notches carved on stone edges.

clue.text: Striker on trial in game

indicators.note: in an across clue the striker goes on after the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A footballer is being tried out in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' looks like a footballer but is a match. A Test match is international cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international game of cricket between national sides.

clue.text: Wrong steering mechanism, we hear, producing spark

indicators.note: this signals words spoken that match a word in sound

parts.note: a wrong is a sin, and a tiller is the lever that steers a boat

explanation.surface: A faulty steering part is said to have caused a spark.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or flash, from Latin for a spark.

clue.text: Calm about key — it's found back in park

indicators.note: the calm word goes around the key

parts.note: serene means calm
G is a musical key

indicators.note: the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A peaceful mood around a key that turns up again in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a national park in Tanzania famous for wildlife migrations.

clue.text: Recover edge to bind frilly lace

indicators.note: the edge holds the other letters, binding them inside

parts.note: a rim is an edge

indicators.note: frilly suggests something ruffled, so the letters of lace are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seamstress wants back the edge used to hem frilly lace.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to get it back, a synonym of recover.

clue.text: No more iodine under boxes

indicators.note: to box is to enclose, so the lower word holds the iodine

parts.note: nether means lower, under
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: No more iodine is stored under the boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like a position for iodine, but it is NETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in replies like 'nor I', the word means also not, the same as no more.

clue.text: Lower part below ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters of below are rearranged

explanation.surface: The lower section lies underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is in the lower part of the body; its innermost part is also called this.

clue.text: Worker with routine guarding grand corporation

parts.note: a worker bee

indicators.note: the routine surrounds the grand, guarding it

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A worker on routine protecting a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jocular word for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation was once slang for a paunch, a protruding stomach from drinking.

clue.text: Strike that's bitter?

definitions.meaning: British slang for beer, and bitter is a British beer

explanation.surface: A blow that tastes bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop means both a heavy blow and, informally, beer such as bitter.

clue.text: Where lots will be close to you in battle

indicators.note: the last of you goes inside battle

parts.note: action is fighting, battle

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of you

explanation.surface: Many soldiers will soon be fighting near you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like many; it is items for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are items offered for sale at a sale by bidding.

clue.text: Taxi driver not even found in city of yellow taxis?

indicators.note: the odd piece is placed within the city

parts.note: NY is New York, famous for its yellow cabs
odd means not even

explanation.surface: A cabbie who is unusual among New York's yellow taxis.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy, Enid Blyton's character, drives a little taxi in Toyland.

clue.text: Error ultimately filed in report is framework for training?

indicators.note: the letter is filed inside report, put in like a document

parts.note: to tell is to report

indicators.note: this takes the last letter of error

explanation.surface: A mistake in a filed report concerns a training framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' means growing plants up a support, not coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice for training climbing plants upward.

clue.text: Destroyed, as are semi-finalist and runner-up?

definitions.meaning: each of these words contains a hyphen, a short dash

explanation.surface: Losing finalists have had their hopes destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are dashed are ruined, and hyphenated words carry little dashes.

clue.text: Othello, say, set about seeking latitude

indicators.note: about means turned round, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice
to gel is to set

explanation.surface: Othello, as an example, is set on looking for latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means room to move freely, the same as space for the legs.

clue.text: Pen circling blot, poor Einstein

indicators.note: the pen goes round the blot

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
to mar is to blot or spoil
pants is British slang for rubbish, poor

explanation.surface: A fountain pen circles an ink blot, a sad end for Einstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Einstein' is used ironically for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: An Einstein is ironic slang for a clever clogs, a know-all who shows off.
